Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **AI Collaboration Rule**:
> - **Planning**, **Brainstorming**, **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** are all
>   in scope. Planning is no longer delegated to Gemini (Antigravity).
> - Implementation plans go in `.claude/plans/` (see
>   [rules/planning.md](rules/planning.md)); design decisions that outlive a plan
>   are recorded in `docs/backlog.md`. Open work (stories, tasks, bugs) is tracked
>   in Plane, see the `## Plane` section of the root `CLAUDE.md`.
> - Always refer to [project-context.md](../project-context.md) for global project rules.
>   It sits in this repository, at the root. The absolute path this line used to
>   carry named a GitLab checkout that is no longer where DevDesk lives.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line), tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost`, from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, or when its transcript is gone (header `Updates › paused`); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

## Architecture

The deep notes live in `docs/architecture/`, one file per area, and they are
**not** `@`-imported: an `@` would inline all of it into every session, which is
the thing this split exists to avoid. Read the file that covers what you are
touching, and update it in the same commit as the code.

| File | Covers |
|---|---|
| [`app-shell.md`](../docs/architecture/app-shell.md) | the router and its views, `ctrl+p` and the command parser, the keyboard vocabulary (`internal/ui/keymap`), greyed shortcuts, `shared.State`, cross-view messages, the jobs registry (`internal/jobs`), the one spinner chain and the `:jobs` view |
| [`configuration.md`](../docs/architecture/configuration.md) | the config schema, the contexts, the migrations (`gitlab:` → `forge:`, `docker:` → `network:`), `agent_usage.prices`, and the configuration view |
| [`forge.md`](../docs/architecture/forge.md) | `internal/forge` and its two backends, `forge.Vocabulary`, the explorer's clone pipeline, and how the explorer reads the forge index (`internal/forgeindex`) and its `g` |
| [`workspaces.md`](../docs/architecture/workspaces.md) | the `ws` file icons (`internal/ui/fileicon`) and the sync (`F`) |
| [`filebrowser.md`](../docs/architecture/filebrowser.md) | `:files` (`internal/ui/filebrowser`, `internal/fsbrowse`), the path picker a form's path field opens with enter, and `theme.ShortPath` |
| [`viewer.md`](../docs/architecture/viewer.md) | `internal/viewer` + `internal/ui/viewer` — kinds, displays, colouring, search, follow |
| [`scanning.md`](../docs/architecture/scanning.md) | Trivy, Gitleaks, plumber, `scan.Categorize`, the `:sec` inventory, the two scan caches, image signatures (`internal/trust`, the cosign verifier) |
| [`registries.md`](../docs/architecture/registries.md) | the registry/group model and the discovered-members cache |
| [`network.md`](../docs/architecture/network.md) | `internal/docker` and `internal/oci`, image updates (`internal/imageupdate`, the Update column), verified pulls (`internal/imagepull`), the netdiag view, `internal/ports`, `internal/netiface` |
| [`mcp.md`](../docs/architecture/mcp.md) | the MCP server the TUI serves over HTTP |
| [`templates.md`](../docs/architecture/templates.md) | `internal/template` + `internal/ui/templates` — the repository-template catalog, its three sources, how files are fetched, and the `:templates` view |
| [`ui-components.md`](../docs/architecture/ui-components.md) | `components.FooterMessage` and `internal/ui/datatable` |
| [`agent-usage.md`](../docs/architecture/agent-usage.md) | `internal/agentusage` — per-agent token counts from Claude Code transcripts: format, aggregation rules, tolerance, privacy (`cwd` amendment), caps, ccusage cross-check; `ListSessions`; incremental reading (`ReadDelta`, `Aggregate`, `Activity.Settled`); tool calls and time span per agent (DEVDESK-46); per-model tokens, `Billed`, and the cost estimate (`internal/agentusage/pricing`, prices from `agent_usage.prices`, DEVDESK-47); the `:agent-usage` view and its agents level and State/Tools/Duration/Est. cost columns; the Breakdown column and tab, `Usage.Categories`/`ModelTotals` (DEVDESK-98) (`internal/ui/agentusageview`) |

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

## Dependencies

Key libraries (see `go.mod`):
- `github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea` - TUI framework
- `github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles` - Pre-built TUI components (table, textinput, spinner)
- `github.com/charmbracelet/lipgloss` - Styling
- `gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go` - GitLab API client
- `github.com/prometheus-community/pro-bing` - ICMP ping functionality (maintained fork of go-ping/ping)
- `github.com/google/go-github/v68` - GitHub API client (§3.6)
- `github.com/libp2p/go-netroute` - which interface a destination leaves by, on all three platforms (§3.44)
- `github.com/zalando/go-keyring` - host secret manager (wincred / Keychain / Secret Service), no cgo
- `gopkg.in/yaml.v3` - YAML configuration

## Code Conventions

- Comments: **English only** (Rule 307) — existing French comments are not rewritten wholesale, but any new or edited comment is in English
- Commit messages: **English only** (Rule 307)
- UI text and logs: **English US only** (Rule 129)
- Bubbletea models define their own message types
- Use `theme` package for consistent styling (`internal/ui/theme/`)
- Config changes must call `config.Save()` to persist
- All colors defined in `theme/colors.go`, all styles in `theme/styles.go`
- Message naming: `[ComponentName][Action]Msg` (e.g., `ComponentFormSubmitMsg`)
- Context names: the rule exists twice (`config.ValidateContextName`, `contextcmd.ValidName`); change both or neither (`TestContextNameRulesAgree`). Creation refuses `-`, `new`, `list` (`config.ValidateNewContextName`); loading does not (D91)

## Critical Bubble Tea Rules

**NEVER modify model state inside a Cmd** (Rule 110) - Race condition:
- `Update()` is the ONLY place to modify model state
- `View()` is read-only
- `Cmd` functions do I/O and return messages

**NEVER use `style.Render()` inside `table.Row{}`** (Rule 122) - ANSI sequences corrupt all subsequent rows:
- Use plain text: `theme.IconError + " error"` not `theme.StatusErrorStyle.Render(...)`
- Apply row styling via `table.SetStyles(theme.TableStylesForState("error"))`

**Update() case extraction**: If a case block exceeds 5 lines, extract to `handle[MessageType]()` method returning `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

# Planning Rules

## Implementation Plans

- **Location**: Always write implementation plans to `.claude/plans/` in the current project directory.
- **Format**: Use Markdown format for plans.
- **Naming**: Use descriptive names like `feature-name-plan.md` or `YYYY-MM-DD-feature-name.md`.

## Antigravity IDE Integration

When using the Antigravity IDE extension:
- Save all implementation plans to `.claude/plans/` relative to the project root.
- Create the directory if it doesn't exist before saving plans.
- Plans should be accessible from both Claude Code CLI and Antigravity IDE.

# TUI — Rule index

TUI rules are split across 5 topic files:

| File | Rules | Content |
|---------|--------|---------|
| [`tui-layout.md`](tui-layout.md) | 101, 107, 108, 111, 112, 123, 124, 130, 134, 137, 138 | General layout, keybindings, viewport, tabs, shortcuts header, format descriptions, shortcuts obviousness |
| [`tui-theme.md`](tui-theme.md) | 102, 105, 115, 117, 118, 119, 127, 129 | Colors, lipgloss background, `theme.*` helpers, language |
| [`tui-forms.md`](tui-forms.md) | 103, 104, 113, 114, 120, 121, 131, 132, 133, 135 | Forms, modals, focus, status icons, value cycling, WrappedInput, key assignment |
| [`tui-tables.md`](tui-tables.md) | 106, 116, 122, 125, 136, 139 | Tables, column widths, plain-text cells + color via `Style`, filter bar, body never replaced (spinner or message) |
| [`tui-behavior.md`](tui-behavior.md) | 109, 110, 126, 128 | Bubble Tea (Cmd/Update), scan cache, footer messages (three levels, one component) |

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer with a spinner, never in the body.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a spinner or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

The per-topic TUI rule files above load when a matching file is read or edited; when reviewing a diff without opening files, read them explicitly.

# entire-graph — instructions for coding agents (follow directly)

You have a deterministic local code graph: `entire graph` (functions, classes, methods,
types, routes + call/inheritance relations; no network). These instructions are FOR YOU, the
agent reading this file. Use the graph to narrow exploration without trading away correctness.

## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"

Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle.

## Hard rules

1. SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before you have searched.
2. READ focused source around the result. Widen the check when aliases, generated code, dynamic
   dispatch, or related implementations could matter.
3. Use graph follow-ups only when they answer a real question. For impact or callers, prefer:
       entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X
4. Make the smallest complete edit and check sibling sites or contracts when the task implies them.
5. VERIFY before stopping. Run the most focused relevant test, build, or reproduction available.
   If execution is unavailable, perform a bounded source-level verification and state the limit.
6. Prefer precise queries and line ranges, but never trade resolution for fewer turns.
7. Feature-detect before relying on semantic relations:
       entire graph capabilities --json

## When NOT to use the graph

If the task already names the exact file and it is small, just read it — the graph saves tokens
by eliminating exploration; when there is nothing to explore, skip it.

## Reference

    locate  ->  entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "..."
    impact  ->  entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X   (one shot: callers, callees, type consumers, data flow, co-change, siblings)
    callers ->  entire graph neighbors --repo . --symbol X --relation CALLS --direction in

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **AI Collaboration Rule**:
> - **Planning**, **Brainstorming**, **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** are all
>   in scope. Planning is no longer delegated to Gemini (Antigravity).
> - Implementation plans go in `.claude/plans/` (see
>   [rules/planning.md](rules/planning.md)); design decisions that outlive a plan
>   are recorded in `docs/backlog.md`. Open work (stories, tasks, bugs) is tracked
>   in Plane, see the `## Plane` section of the root `CLAUDE.md`.
> - Always refer to [project-context.md](../project-context.md) for global project rules.
>   It sits in this repository, at the root. The absolute path this line used to
>   carry named a GitLab checkout that is no longer where DevDesk lives.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line), tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost`, from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, or when its transcript is gone (header `Updates › paused`); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

## Dependencies

Key libraries (see `go.mod`):
- `github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea` - TUI framework
- `github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles` - Pre-built TUI components (table, textinput, spinner)
- `github.com/charmbracelet/lipgloss` - Styling
- `gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go` - GitLab API client
- `github.com/prometheus-community/pro-bing` - ICMP ping functionality (maintained fork of go-ping/ping)
- `github.com/google/go-github/v68` - GitHub API client (§3.6)
- `github.com/libp2p/go-netroute` - which interface a destination leaves by, on all three platforms (§3.44)
- `github.com/zalando/go-keyring` - host secret manager (wincred / Keychain / Secret Service), no cgo
- `gopkg.in/yaml.v3` - YAML configuration

## Code Conventions

- Comments: **English only** (Rule 307) — existing French comments are not rewritten wholesale, but any new or edited comment is in English
- Commit messages: **English only** (Rule 307)
- UI text and logs: **English US only** (Rule 129)
- Bubbletea models define their own message types
- Use `theme` package for consistent styling (`internal/ui/theme/`)
- Config changes must call `config.Save()` to persist
- All colors defined in `theme/colors.go`, all styles in `theme/styles.go`
- Message naming: `[ComponentName][Action]Msg` (e.g., `ComponentFormSubmitMsg`)
- Context names: the rule exists twice (`config.ValidateContextName`, `contextcmd.ValidName`); change both or neither (`TestContextNameRulesAgree`). Creation refuses `-`, `new`, `list` (`config.ValidateNewContextName`); loading does not (D91)

## Critical Bubble Tea Rules

**NEVER modify model state inside a Cmd** (Rule 110) - Race condition:
- `Update()` is the ONLY place to modify model state
- `View()` is read-only
- `Cmd` functions do I/O and return messages

**NEVER use `style.Render()` inside `table.Row{}`** (Rule 122) - ANSI sequences corrupt all subsequent rows:
- Use plain text: `theme.IconError + " error"` not `theme.StatusErrorStyle.Render(...)`
- Apply row styling via `table.SetStyles(theme.TableStylesForState("error"))`

**Update() case extraction**: If a case block exceeds 5 lines, extract to `handle[MessageType]()` method returning `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

TUI rules are split across 5 topic files:

| File | Rules | Content |
|---------|--------|---------|
| [`tui-layout.md`](tui-layout.md) | 101, 107, 108, 111, 112, 123, 124, 130, 134, 137, 138 | General layout, keybindings, viewport, tabs, shortcuts header, format descriptions, shortcuts obviousness |

| [`tui-forms.md`](tui-forms.md) | 103, 104, 113, 114, 120, 121, 131, 132, 133, 135 | Forms, modals, focus, status icons, value cycling, WrappedInput, key assignment |
| [`tui-tables.md`](tui-tables.md) | 106, 116, 122, 125, 136, 139 | Tables, column widths, plain-text cells + color via `Style`, filter bar, body never replaced (spinner or message) |
| [`tui-behavior.md`](tui-behavior.md) | 109, 110, 126, 128 | Bubble Tea (Cmd/Update), scan cache, footer messages (three levels, one component) |

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer with a spinner, never in the body.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a spinner or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

The per-topic TUI rule files above load when a matching file is read or edited; when reviewing a diff without opening files, read them explicitly.

## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"

Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle.

1. SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before you have searched.

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

>   It sits in this repository, at the root. The absolute path this line used to
>   carry named a GitLab checkout that is no longer where DevDesk lives.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line), tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost`, from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, or when its transcript is gone (header `Updates › paused`); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

# DEVDESK-150 (A-12) — netdiag Ports: activity column for the kill

Story: `docs/product/activity-indicator/stories.md` §A-12. UX: `ux.md` §1 (glyphs), §5 (legend).
Worktree: `.worktrees/feat/DEVDESK-150-netdiag-ports-activity` (base `e037b2f`).
Pattern: DEVDESK-146 (OCI images, the closest twin: a `busy` action, `MarkBusy`/`ClearBusy`,
reported as `Observed: Running` through `components.DescribeRow`), DEVDESK-148/149 (guard, help).

**What makes this story small.** The Ports table has no registry run at all: its only row
operation is `K` (SIGKILL), held in `datatable`'s `busy` map, keyed by PID. `datatable` already
writes the precedence "busy ⇒ `indicator.Running`" once (`render.go::indicatorState`), so the
view only adds an `IndicatorColumn` whose own state is always `Idle`. `jobs.ChangedMsg`,
`jobs.ForgetTarget`, `FailureEvent` and the failure memory are **not used**: nothing here goes
through the registry, and the kill failure stays a footer `Error` (criterion 1, D5: there is no
kill kind to remember).

Out of scope: `H`, the Diagnostics (checks) and Interfaces tables, the Forward tab, `internal/ports`.

## Finding in the current code (fixed by the story itself)

`portsSpinnerTickMsg` is not routed by `netdiag.Model.Update` (`update.go:90` lists
`portsTickMsg, portsDataMsg, portsKillResultMsg` only): the tick lands in the fall-through and
is dropped, so in production the row spinner shows frame 0 and never turns.
`TestTheKillSpinnerTickStopsWhenTheKillLands` calls `handleSpinnerTick` directly and does not see it.
The story deletes the chain; no separate bug.

## Blocking questions (user)

| # | Question | Options | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Q1 | **Open question 4 of `stories.md`: a network test that fails** (TCP refused, invalid TLS) — row result or remembered operation failure? | **A** result: it stays in the Verdict column of the checks table, nothing changes there; the red dot is reserved for an operation that failed (criterion 4 as written) · **B** remembered failure: a `⊗` and the failure memory for a diagnostic, which needs a column on the checks table, a kind in the registry, and is no longer an S story | **A**: the Verdict already says FAIL in red with its reason; a `⊗` on top would say the same thing twice, and "the check could not look" (UNKNOWN) is a result too. The plan is written for A (criterion 4 = a regression test). B would be a new story. |
| Q2 | **What the State cell shows during a kill.** Today the State cell is replaced by the spinner (§3.22: "the row must not show the state the signal is about to change"; `TestAKillSpinsTheSocketState` pins it). With the dot in column 0 that replacement goes (`StatusColumn` is a retired mechanism). | **A** State keeps its text, dimmed like every busy row (`datatable.cellStyle` busy branch, no view code; same as OCI images after DEVDESK-146) · **B** State reads `killing` (dim) while busy, from a `Cell` that checks `IsBusy` (the view reads the busy map in a cell: a second path to the same fact) · **C** State blank while busy | **A**: the dot says "in progress", the dim says "ceasing to be true" (the datatable comment's wording), and one alphabet with OCI. It reverses the letter of §3.22 (LISTEN visible, dim) but keeps its intent. |

## Hypotheses (prudent default, no question)

- H1 **Column 0** = `datatable.IndicatorColumn(func(ports.Socket) indicator.State { return indicator.Idle }, nil, nil)`:
  no rest icon (the row has none), so an idle row shows an empty two-cell column. A busy row is
  `Running` through `datatable`'s precedence: every socket of the PID shows `●`/`○` (today's
  "every row of that process spins" kept).
- H2 **The blink phase comes from `jobs.FrameMsg`** handled by `netdiag.Model.Update`:
  `m.portsModel.table.SetBlinkPhase(msg.Blink)`, nothing rebuilt. **The footers' spinner frames
  are not touched**: the Diagnostics run and the Interfaces load keep their own `spinner.TickMsg`
  chain (D2, criterion 5).
- H3 **`WantsBlink()`** (router's `BlinkingView`) on `*netdiag.Model` = `len(m.portsModel.table.BusyLabels()) > 0`,
  whatever the active tab (a level; the router only frames the view on screen; a kill lasts a moment).
- H4 **Per-row footer** (A-05): `PortsModel.statusLine()` adds `Detail` = `components.DescribeRow(RowQuery{Observed: indicator.Running, ObservedText: label}).Detail`
  when the selected row's PID is busy (label = the existing `"Killing <process> (<pid>)"`), zero
  otherwise. Text/Level (stale error, paused) unchanged and placed after the detail by
  `RowStatusLine`. At 60 columns this is where the process name is readable (PID and Process
  columns are dropped there).
- H5 **Kill outcomes unchanged**: success `Info` "Process N terminated", failure `Error`
  `killFailureMessage` (§3.49, D5), `ClearBusy` on both; the row returns to rest (no `⊗`).
  `K` stays lit on a busy row (Rule 130: an operation in progress is not a reason to grey);
  `Already killing PID N` warning kept.
- H6 **The periodic refresh never blinks** (criterion 3): `SetItems` does not touch `busy`; a
  refresh with nothing busy leaves every column-0 cell empty and `WantsBlink()` false.
- H7 **Scan scope of the guard**: the I/O commands (`fetchPortsCmd`, `portsTickCmd`,
  `killProcessCmd`, `defaultPortsRefresh`, `portsFetchTimeout`) move to a new
  `internal/ui/netdiag/ports_commands.go`, **not scanned**, exactly like OCI's `commands.go`
  (its refresh `tea.Tick` is data, not a row animation). Scanned: `ports_model.go`,
  `ports_activity.go`, `header.go`, `update.go`. `forward_model.go` (its own refresh tick) and the
  other tabs are not scanned (not migrated). Alternative rejected: an entry in
  `declaredViewTicks`, documented as "empty today, may only shrink".
- H8 **Guard footer seed**: the seed must not read the real socket table nor kill anything. It
  needs an exported way to hand rows to the view: `func NewPortsDataMsg(sockets []ports.Socket) tea.Msg`
  in `ports_commands.go` (returns the unexported `portsDataMsg`; no rename, no test churn). The
  seed drives the view's `Update` directly (not the router: the Init `Cmd` and the kill `Cmd` are
  never executed), with a PID that cannot exist on Linux (`"4194305"` > `pid_max`).
- H9 `TestDeclaredRowChainsLogic` keeps its fictitious `ports_model.go` fixtures (its own local
  pending list); the `portsSpinnerCmd` detector in `TestRowAnimationChainsOutsideTheRouterAreDeclared`
  stays (it now catches a reintroduction).

## Width arithmetic (Rule 116; `cellPadding = 2`; inside = width − 2)

Columns (min + 2): dot 4, Proto 8, State 12, Local 28, Peer 28, PID 9, Process 12. None is
`Optional`, so required columns give way rightmost first. With addresses at their 26-cell floor:

| Columns shown | today from width | after from width |
|---|---|---|
| all | 99 | **103** |
| without Process | 87 | **91** |
| without PID, Process | 78 | **82** |
| dot, Proto, State, Local | 50 | **54** |

At 60: dot, Proto, State, Local Address (same set as today), `RenderedWidth() == 58`. These are
estimates: the tester pins them with the sweep of step 1; the measured values go into `network.md`.

## Steps (TDD — tests first; each step green and mergeable alone)

Base command: `go test ./internal/ui/netdiag/ ./internal/app/ && go vet ./...`.
Step 3 adds `mise run lint`, `go test -count=2 ./internal/app/`, `mise run test-race`.

### Step 1 — Activity column, row chain removed, blink, refresh · S

Files: `internal/ui/netdiag/ports_model.go` (columns, config, update, kill), new
`ports_commands.go` (H7, moved code + `NewPortsDataMsg`), new `ports_activity.go`, `update.go`
(`jobs.FrameMsg` case), tests `ports_model_test.go` (+ new `ports_activity_test.go`).

1	# DEVDESK-150 (A-12) — netdiag Ports: activity column for the kill
2	
3	Story: `docs/product/activity-indicator/stories.md` §A-12. UX: `ux.md` §1 (glyphs), §5 (legend).
4	Worktree: `.worktrees/feat/DEVDESK-150-netdiag-ports-activity` (base `e037b2f`).
5	Pattern: DEVDESK-146 (OCI images, the closest twin: a `busy` action, `MarkBusy`/`ClearBusy`,
6	reported as `Observed: Running` through `components.DescribeRow`), DEVDESK-148/149 (guard, help).
7	
8	**What makes this story small.** The Ports table has no registry run at all: its only row
9	operation is `K` (SIGKILL), held in `datatable`'s `busy` map, keyed by PID. `datatable` already
10	writes the precedence "busy ⇒ `indicator.Running`" once (`render.go::indicatorState`), so the
11	view only adds an `IndicatorColumn` whose own state is always `Idle`. `jobs.ChangedMsg`,
12	`jobs.ForgetTarget`, `FailureEvent` and the failure memory are **not used**: nothing here goes
13	through the registry, and the kill failure stays a footer `Error` (criterion 1, D5: there is no
14	kill kind to remember).
15	
16	Out of scope: `H`, the Diagnostics (checks) and Interfaces tables, the Forward tab, `internal/ports`.
17	
18	## Finding in the current code (fixed by the story itself)
19	
20	`portsSpinnerTickMsg` is not routed by `netdiag.Model.Update` (`update.go:90` lists
21	`portsTickMsg, portsDataMsg, portsKillResultMsg` only): the tick lands in the fall-through and
22	is dropped, so in production the row spinner shows frame 0 and never turns.
23	`TestTheKillSpinnerTickStopsWhenTheKillLands` calls `handleSpinnerTick` directly and does not see it.
24	The story deletes the chain; no separate bug.
25	
26	## Blocking questions (user)
27	
28	| # | Question | Options | Recommendation |
29	|---|---|---|---|
30	| Q1 | **Open question 4 of `stories.md`: a network test that fails** (TCP refused, invalid TLS) — row result or remembered operation failure? | **A** result: it stays in the Verdict column of the checks table, nothing changes there; the red dot is reserved for an operation that failed (criterion 4 as written) · **B** remembered failure: a `⊗` and the failure memory for a diagnostic, which needs a column on the checks table, a kind in the registry, and is no longer an S story | **A**: the Verdict already says FAIL in red with its reason; a `⊗` on top would say the same thing twice, and "the check could not look" (UNKNOWN) is a result too. The plan is written for A (criterion 4 = a regression test). B would be a new story. |
31	| Q2 | **What the State cell shows during a kill.** Today the State cell is replaced by the spinner (§3.22: "the row must not show the state the signal is about to change"; `TestAKillSpinsTheSocketState` pins it). With the dot in column 0 that replacement goes (`StatusColumn` is a retired mechanism). | **A** State keeps its text, dimmed like every busy row (`datatable.cellStyle` busy branch, no view code; same as OCI images after DEVDESK-146) · **B** State reads `killing` (dim) while busy, from a `Cell` that checks `IsBusy` (the view reads the busy map in a cell: a second path to the same fact) · **C** State blank while busy | **A**: the dot says "in progress", the dim says "ceasing to be true" (the datatable comment's wording), and one alphabet with OCI. It reverses the letter of §3.22 (LISTEN visible, dim) but keeps its intent. |
32	
33	## Hypotheses (prudent default, no question)
34	
35	- H1 **Column 0** = `datatable.IndicatorColumn(func(ports.Socket) indicator.State { return indicator.Idle }, nil, nil)`:
36	  no rest icon (the row has none), so an idle row shows an empty two-cell column. A busy row is
37	  `Running` through `datatable`'s precedence: every socket of the PID shows `●`/`○` (today's
38	  "every row of that process spins" kept).
39	- H2 **The blink phase comes from `jobs.FrameMsg`** handled by `netdiag.Model.Update`:
40	  `m.portsModel.table.SetBlinkPhase(msg.Blink)`, nothing rebuilt. **The footers' spinner frames
41	  are not touched**: the Diagnostics run and the Interfaces load keep their own `spinner.TickMsg`

# MCP Server Instructions

The following MCP servers have provided instructions for how to use their tools and resources:

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>\n\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\n\n<?claude block s1?>\n\n<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. 159	
160	// portStateStyle colours the socket state, which is the column this table is
161	// scanned down: a listening port is something the machine offers, an
162	// established one is a conversation in progress, and everything else is a
163	// socket on its way out.
164	func portStateStyle(p ports.Socket) lipgloss.Style {
165		switch strings.ToUpper(p.State) {
166		case "LISTEN":
167			return theme.StatusOKStyle
168		case "ESTAB", "ESTABLISHED":
169			return lipgloss.NewStyle().Foreground(theme.ColorHighlight)
170		case "":
171			return theme.DimStyle
172		default: // TIME-WAIT, CLOSE-WAIT, SYN-SENT — transient, and not the point
173			return theme.DimStyle
174		}
175	}
176	
177	// matchPortTokens applies the toggle filters: OR within a group, AND between
178	// them. `numeric` and `paused` are shown in the bar but filter nothing — they
179	// report a mode, which is why they are not consulted here.
180	func matchPortTokens(p ports.Socket, active map[string]bool) bool {
181		return matchesActive(p.Protocol, active, filterTokenTCP, filterTokenUDP) &&
182			matchesActive(p.State, active, filterTokenListen, filterTokenEstab)
183	}
184	
185	// matchesActive reports whether value equals one of the labels the user turned
186	// on. A group with nothing on does not filter: that is "no opinion", not
187	// "match nothing", and getting the two confused would empty the table on open.
188	func matchesActive(value string, active map[string]bool, labels ...string) bool {
189		anyOn := false
190		for _, label := range labels {
191			if !active[label] {
192				continue
193			}
194			anyOn = true
195			if strings.EqualFold(value, label) {
196				return true
197			}
198		}
199		return !anyOn
200	}

202	// newPortsModel creates a new PortsModel.
203	func newPortsModel(refresh time.Duration) *PortsModel {
204		return &PortsModel{
205			refresh:      refresh,
206			numericAddrs: true,
207			table: datatable.New(datatable.Config[ports.Socket]{
208				Columns:    portsColumns(),
209				SortColumn: -1, // the order ss reports is the order shown
210				Tokens: []components.FilterToken{
211					{Label: filterTokenTCP},
212					{Label: filterTokenUDP},
213					{Label: filterTokenListen},
214					{Label: filterTokenEstab},
215					{Label: filterTokenNumeric},
216					{Label: filterTokenPaused},
217				},
218				TokenMatch: matchPortTokens,
219				// A PID, not a socket: killing a process takes every socket it
220				// holds, so every one of its rows spins together — which is what
221				// actually happens.
222				Key: func(p ports.Socket) string { return p.PID },
223			}),

244		}

255			return pm.handleData(msg)
256		case portsKillResultMsg:
257			return pm.handleKillResult(msg)
258		case components.ConfirmModalYesMsg:
259			pm.confirmModal = nil
260			return pm.killSelected()
261		case components.ConfirmModalNoMsg:
262			pm.confirmModal = nil
263			return pm, nil
264		case tea.KeyMsg:
265			return pm.handleKey(msg)
266		}
267		return pm, nil
268	}
269	
270	func (pm *PortsModel) handleTick() (*PortsModel, tea.Cmd) {
271		if pm.paused {
272			return pm, portsTickCmd(pm.refresh)
273		}
274		return pm, tea.Batch(fetchPortsCmd(pm.numericAddrs), portsTickCmd(pm.refresh))
275	}
276	
277	func (pm *PortsModel) handleData(msg portsDataMsg) (*PortsModel, tea.Cmd) {
278		if msg.err != nil {
279			log.Printf("ERROR [netdiag/ports] ports.List: %v", msg.err)
280			// The rows stay: they are dated, not wrong, and the status line is what
281			// says so. No footer message — this is a state, and a state that
282			// expires after three seconds is how a dead table came to look alive.
283			pm.stale = true
284			return pm, nil
285		}
286		pm.stale = false
287		pm.lastOK = time.Now()
288		// The cursor and the scroll survive this, which is what the whole
289		// tableReady dance existed to achieve on a two-second tick.
290		pm.table.SetItems(msg.ports)
291		return pm, nil
292	}
293	
294	func (pm *PortsModel) handleKillResult(msg portsKillResultMsg) (*PortsModel, tea.Cmd) {
295		// On every outcome: a kill that failed has to let the socket state show
296		// again rather than go on turning.
297		pm.table.ClearBusy(msg.pid)
298		if msg.err != nil {
299			log.Printf("ERROR [netdiag/ports] ports.Kill pid=%s: %v", msg.pid, msg.err)
300			return pm, pm.footer.Error(killFailureMessage(msg.pid, msg.err))
301		}
302		return pm, pm.footer.Info(fmt.Sprintf("Process %s terminated", msg.pid))
303	}
304	
305	// killFailureMessage says why the signal did not land.
306	//
307	// DevDesk signals with the rights it has (§3.43), so the refusal the user meets
308	// most often is the operating system's — another user's process, a service, one
309	// Windows protects. "Failed to kill PID 1234" gave them no reason to suspect
310	// that, and made "access denied" and "already gone" the same sentence.
311	//
312	// The platform error itself never reaches the screen: it comes back in the
313	// machine's own language — measured here, PID 4 answers `OpenProcess: Accès
314	// refusé.` — which is the route stage's rule (§3.44). errors.Is reads through
315	// the %w wrapping ports.Kill applies, and both sentinels are the standard
316	// library's.
317	//
318	// The permission branch was measured on Windows: killing PID 4 (System) gives
319	// ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED, which syscall.Errno maps onto os.ErrPermission. EPERM
320	// maps the same way on Unix.
321	//
322	// **The "already gone" branch does not fire on Windows**, and that is measured
323	// too: a PID that does not exist fails OpenProcess with
324	// ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER, which maps to neither sentinel, so it falls to the
325	// generic message. Mapping that code would be a guess — it is what an invalid
326	// argument returns as well — and the row disappears on the next two-second
327	// refresh anyway. The branch is kept because ESRCH does map to
328	// os.ErrProcessDone on Unix.
329	func killFailureMessage(pid string, err error) string {
330		switch {
331		case errors.Is(err, os.ErrPermission):
332			return fmt.Sprintf("Refused by the system — DevDesk cannot signal PID %s", pid)
333		case errors.Is(err, os.ErrProcessDone):
334			return fmt.Sprintf("PID %s is no longer running", pid)
335		}
336		return fmt.Sprintf("Failed to kill PID %s — check logs", pid)
337	}
338	
339	func (pm *PortsModel) handleKey(msg tea.KeyMsg) (*PortsModel, tea.Cmd) {
340		if pm.confirmModal != nil {
341			var cmd tea.Cmd
342			pm.confirmModal, cmd = pm.confirmModal.Update(msg)
343			return pm, cmd
344		}
345		if pm.table.InEditMode() {
346			cmd := pm.table.Update(msg)
347			pm.table.GotoTop() // a narrowing query starts from the first match
348			return pm, cmd
349		}
350		return pm.handleKeyNormal(msg)
351	}
352	
353	// toggleToken flips a filter and returns to the top, since the list under the
354	// cursor is not the list the user was looking at any more.
355	func (pm *PortsModel) toggleToken(label string) {
356		pm.table.SetTokenActive(label, !pm.table.IsTokenActive(label))
357		pm.table.GotoTop()
358	}
359	
360	func (pm *PortsModel) handleKeyNormal(msg tea.KeyMsg) (*PortsModel, tea.Cmd) {
361		switch msg.String() {
362		case "up", "down", "pgup", "pgdown", "home", "end", "/":
363			return pm, pm.table.Update(msg)
364		case " ":
365			pm.paused = !pm.paused
366			pm.table.SetTokenActive(filterTokenPaused, pm.paused)
367			// Pausing is a state, not an event: it is derived in statusLine rather
368			// than set as a message, which would expire while still paused.
369		case "t":
370			pm.toggleToken(filterTokenTCP)
371		case "u":
372			pm.toggleToken(filterTokenUDP)
373		case "l":
374			pm.toggleToken(filterTokenListen)
375		case "e":
376			pm.toggleToken(filterTokenEstab)
377		case "n":
378			pm.numericAddrs = !pm.numericAddrs
379			pm.table.SetTokenActive(filterTokenNumeric, pm.numericAddrs)
380			return pm, fetchPortsCmd(pm.numericAddrs)
381		case "z":
382			for _, label := range []string{
383				filterTokenTCP, filterTokenUDP, filterTokenListen, filterTokenEstab, filterTokenPaused,
384			} {
385				pm.table.SetTokenActive(label, false)
386			}
387			pm.table.FilterBar().ClearSearch()
388			pm.table.SetItems(pm.table.Items()) // re-apply with the query gone
389			pm.paused = false
390			pm.table.GotoTop()
391		case keymap.Kill:
392			return pm.confirmKill()
393		}
394		return pm, nil
395	}
396	
397	// confirmKill asks before sending the signal.
398	//
399	// This is the one action in the application that reaches outside it: not a
400	// container to be brought back up, but a process belonging to whoever is at
401	// this machine, killed with SIGKILL so it gets no chance to save anything. It
402	// had no confirmation at all, while deleting a container — recreatable from its
403	// image — had one (§3.26).
404	func (pm *PortsModel) confirmKill() (*PortsModel, tea.Cmd) {
405		if k := pm.killable(); !k.Enabled() {
406			return pm, pm.footer.Warn(k.Reason)
407		}
408		entry, _ := pm.table.Selected()
409		if pm.table.IsBusy(entry.PID) {
410			return pm, pm.footer.Warn("Already killing PID " + entry.PID)
411		}
412		pm.confirmModal = components.NewConfirmModal(
413			"Kill Process",
414			fmt.Sprintf("Send SIGKILL to %s (PID %s)?\n\nThe process gets no chance to shut down cleanly.",
415				entry.Process, entry.PID),
416		)
417		return pm, nil
418	}
419	
420	// Why K does not apply, written once so the header, the footer and the tests
421	// cannot drift apart on the wording (Rule 129 — English US).
422	const (
423		reasonNoSocketRow = "No socket selected"
424		reasonNoPID       = "The system did not say which process holds this socket"
425	)
426	
427	// killable reports whether K has a process to signal (Rule 130).
428	//
429	// A socket the system declines to attribute carries no PID — `List` blanks a
430	// PID of zero rather than printing it, because process 0 is a whole process
431	// group on Unix and a row reading "0" would look killable. That is the state
432	// this greys; whether the operating system will *accept* the signal is a
433	// different question, and one only the attempt can answer.
434	func (pm *PortsModel) killable() shortcut.Availability {
435		entry, ok := pm.table.Selected()
436		switch {
437		case !ok:
438			return shortcut.Unavailable(reasonNoSocketRow)
439		case entry.PID == "":
440			return shortcut.Unavailable(reasonNoPID)
441		}
442		return shortcut.Availability{}
443	}
444	
445	// killSelected sends the signal, once confirmed.
446	func (pm *PortsModel) killSelected() (*PortsModel, tea.Cmd) {
447		entry, ok := pm.table.Selected()
448		if !ok {
449			return pm, nil
450		}
451		if entry.PID == "" || pm.table.IsBusy(entry.PID) {
452			return pm, nil
453		}
454		// Keyed on the PID, so every socket the process holds shows the running dot
455		// at once — which is what happens: the kill takes them all. The table reads
456		// the busy mark at render; the router's frame drives the blink.
457		pm.table.MarkBusy(entry.PID, "Killing "+entry.Process+" ("+entry.PID+")")
458		return pm, killProcessCmd(entry.PID)
459	}
460	
461	// view renders the table. An empty table stays a table (Rule 139) — its
462	// header and no rows — whether it is genuinely empty, filtered down to
463	// nothing, still loading, or stale: those are a footer status (statusLine) and
464	// a header count, never body text.
465	func (pm *PortsModel) view() string {
466		return pm.table.View()
467	}
468	
469	// summaryLine counts what is on screen, for the header (Rule 139).
470	func (pm *PortsModel) summaryLine() string {
471		return fmt.Sprintf("%d", len(pm.table.Items()))
472	}

# entire-graph — instructions for coding agents (follow directly)

You have a deterministic local code graph: `entire graph` (functions, classes, methods,
types, routes + call/inheritance relations; no network). These instructions are FOR YOU, the
agent reading this file. Use the graph to narrow exploration without trading away correctness.

## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"

Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle.

## Hard rules

1. SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before you have searched.
2. READ focused source around the result. Widen the check when aliases, generated code, dynamic
   dispatch, or related implementations could matter.
3. Use graph follow-ups only when they answer a real question. For impact or callers, prefer:
       entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X
4. Make the smallest complete edit and check sibling sites or contracts when the task implies them.
5. VERIFY before stopping. Run the most focused relevant test, build, or reproduction available.
   If execution is unavailable, perform a bounded source-level verification and state the limit.
6. Prefer precise queries and line ranges, but never trade resolution for fewer turns.
7. Feature-detect before relying on semantic relations:
       entire graph capabilities --json

## When NOT to use the graph

If the task already names the exact file and it is small, just read it — the graph saves tokens
by eliminating exploration; when there is nothing to explore, skip it.

## Reference

    locate  ->  entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "..."

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **AI Collaboration Rule**:
> - **Planning**, **Brainstorming**, **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** are all
>   in scope. Planning is no longer delegated to Gemini (Antigravity).
> - Implementation plans go in `.claude/plans/` (see
>   [rules/planning.md](rules/planning.md)); design decisions that outlive a plan
>   are recorded in `docs/backlog.md`. Open work (stories, tasks, bugs) is tracked
>   in Plane, see the `## Plane` section of the root `CLAUDE.md`.
> - Always refer to [project-context.md](../project-context.md) for global project rules.
>   It sits in this repository, at the root. The absolute path this line used to
>   carry named a GitLab checkout that is no longer where DevDesk lives.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line), tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost`, from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, or when its transcript is gone (header `Updates › paused`); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

## Architecture

The deep notes live in `docs/architecture/`, one file per area, and they are
**not** `@`-imported: an `@` would inline all of it into every session, which is
the thing this split exists to avoid. Read the file that covers what you are
touching, and update it in the same commit as the code.

| File | Covers |
|---|---|
| [`app-shell.md`](../docs/architecture/app-shell.md) | the router and its views, `ctrl+p` and the command parser, the keyboard vocabulary (`internal/ui/keymap`), greyed shortcuts, `shared.State`, cross-view messages, the jobs registry (`internal/jobs`), the one spinner chain and the `:jobs` view |
| [`configuration.md`](../docs/architecture/configuration.md) | the config schema, the contexts, the migrations (`gitlab:` → `forge:`, `docker:` → `network:`), `agent_usage.prices`, and the configuration view |
| [`forge.md`](../docs/architecture/forge.md) | `internal/forge` and its two backends, `forge.Vocabulary`, the explorer's clone pipeline, and how the explorer reads the forge index (`internal/forgeindex`) and its `g` |
| [`workspaces.md`](../docs/architecture/workspaces.md) | the `ws` file icons (`internal/ui/fileicon`) and the sync (`F`) |
| [`filebrowser.md`](../docs/architecture/filebrowser.md) | `:files` (`internal/ui/filebrowser`, `internal/fsbrowse`), the path picker a form's path field opens with enter, and `theme.ShortPath` |
| [`viewer.md`](../docs/architecture/viewer.md) | `internal/viewer` + `internal/ui/viewer` — kinds, displays, colouring, search, follow |
| [`scanning.md`](../docs/architecture/scanning.md) | Trivy, Gitleaks, plumber, `scan.Categorize`, the `:sec` inventory, the two scan caches, image signatures (`internal/trust`, the cosign verifier) |
| [`registries.md`](../docs/architecture/registries.md) | the registry/group model and the discovered-members cache |
| [`network.md`](../docs/architecture/network.md) | `internal/docker` and `internal/oci`, image updates (`internal/imageupdate`, the Update column), verified pulls (`internal/imagepull`), the netdiag view, `internal/ports`, `internal/netiface` |
| [`mcp.md`](../docs/architecture/mcp.md) | the MCP server the TUI serves over HTTP |
| [`templates.md`](../docs/architecture/templates.md) | `internal/template` + `internal/ui/templates` — the repository-template catalog, its three sources, how files are fetched, and the `:templates` view |
| [`ui-components.md`](../docs/architecture/ui-components.md) | `components.FooterMessage` and `internal/ui/datatable` |
| [`agent-usage.md`](../docs/architecture/agent-usage.md) | `internal/agentusage` — per-agent token counts from Claude Code transcripts: format, aggregation rules, tolerance, privacy (`cwd` amendment), caps, ccusage cross-check; `ListSessions`; incremental reading (`ReadDelta`, `Aggregate`, `Activity.Settled`); tool calls and time span per agent (DEVDESK-46); per-model tokens, `Billed`, and the cost estimate (`internal/agentusage/pricing`, prices from `agent_usage.prices`, DEVDESK-47); the `:agent-usage` view and its agents level and State/Tools/Duration/Est. cost columns; the Breakdown column and tab, `Usage.Categories`/`ModelTotals` (DEVDESK-98) (`internal/ui/agentusageview`) |

### Status Monitoring System

- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
